newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: C.BANK IMPOSES STRICTER REQUIRED RESERVES RULE.
newsitem.headline: C.BANK IMPOSES STRICTER REQUIRED RESERVES RULE.

text.p: Lithuania's central bank said on Thursday that its board decided to impose stricter rules on the required reserves calculation for commercial banks.

"By the new regulations non-resident deposits and resident deposits in non-convertible currencies will have to be included into the calculation of required reserves," Gitanas Nauseda, the head of the bank's policy department, told Reuters.
The new regulations will be introduced gradually starting from August 13, 1997, Nauseda said.
"Non-resident deposits will have to be included in the calculation of required reserves from the beginning of 1998," Nauseda said.
"Requirements for reserves are efficient money market regulation and inflation dampening tools and also help banks to stay liquid," Nauseda added.
